findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects in this reports bucket are stored without enforced server-side encryption (no KMS/SSE default). Sensitive report data could be exposed if the underlying storage or a copy is accessed.
The bucket declares no ACL and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block / policy restrictions, so bucket and object ACLs or policies could grant anonymous public read/write access without any guardrail.

Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) can be overwritten or permanently deleted with no recoverable prior version, aiding destructive tampering or ransomware.
No logging block is configured, so reads and writes to this bucket are not recorded, removing the audit trail needed to detect unauthorized data access.
This ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial export data is stored without an enforced default encryption key.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy = true, meaning ledger export objects can be silently overwritten or destroyed with no prior version retained for integrity verification.
No logging block is configured for this ledger bucket, so access to financial data is not auditable.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource protects this bucket; the 'private' ACL alone does not prevent a later bucket policy or object ACL from exposing the data publicly.
The model artifacts bucket defines versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving stored artifacts unencrypted by default.
No public access block is associated with this bucket, so ACL or policy misconfiguration could expose model artifacts anonymously.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is set, so operational runbooks (which commonly contain hostnames, procedures, and occasionally secrets) are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
This bucket has no logging block, so access to runbook content is not recorded in the audit_trail bucket like other buckets.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket, leaving it one policy change away from public exposure.
The audit log destination bucket has no public access block, so a policy or ACL change could expose security logs publicly; audit log stores should be the most tightly restricted.

The audit log bucket sets force_destroy = true and has no object lock / MFA delete or lifecycle immutability, so log evidence can be deleted by an attacker or by a terraform destroy, undermining forensic integrity.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party contact/PII data) is uploaded into reports_archive, a bucket with no default encryption, no versioning, and no public access block, and the object itself specifies no server_side_encryption or KMS key.
